_readme: THE OPERATIONS REGISTER — [pipeline O-1] Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/14-operations.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
Every failure this factory can suffer, every recurring duty it performs, every surface it serves,
every revert path, every recovery drill, every expiring thing and every retention obligation — each
with a detector, a response, an owner, a cadence and a date. One person cannot hold this; a file can.
WHY IT EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS THE SIXTH REGISTER RATHER THAN A SECTION OF ONE OF THE OTHER FIVE.
Eighteen of stage 14's twenty-one acceptance criteria quantify over 'the operations register'. Until
this file landed that set did not exist (`ls tooling/ops` -> No such file or directory), so all
eighteen ranged over nothing and reported clean. An undefined right-hand side cannot reject anything.
The other five registers answer different questions and are read by other stages' guards:
tooling/capability-register.json  — what shared capability exists and who consumes it   [2]/[3]
tooling/channel-register.json     — what channel is SERVED and with which identity      [9]/[10]
tooling/screen-register.json      — which non-app-specific screens ship in the chassis   [2]/[5]
tooling/platform-register.json    — the shared server's routes and bindings              [4]
tooling/dod-register.json         — the definition of done, per app                      [6]
tooling/monitor-register.json     — every HOSTNAME served, and whether anything watches it [11]
tooling/ceilings.json             — the sourced free-tier ceilings the budgets derive from [4]
Merging this one into any of them would put four other stages' guards on the same file.
🔴 AND THIS REGISTER HOLDS NO HOSTNAMES, ON PURPOSE — THE ONE PLACE IT NEARLY BECAME A SECOND
SOURCE OF TRUTH. Its first draft carried six `surface` rows, one per live hostname, each restating
which GlitchTip monitor watches it and which two are unwatched. [11]E-9's monitor-register.json had
landed the same day with the same facts and a WIDER derivation (Worker custom domains ∪ the app
catalogue ∪ every site's canonical URL, against custom domains alone here) — and its own header says
"[14]O-2 must CONSUME this register rather than re-enumerate the hostnames". Two registers of one set
drift the first time a canonical URL moves and nobody edits both. The rows were CUT and
`_delegated.hostnames` replaces them: assert-ops-register.mjs refuses to run if that file is absent,
unparseable, empty, or blind to a custom domain this repo deploys. Delegation that cannot fail is
just an absence with better manners.
WHY THE PUBLIC REPO AND NOT Private/. CI cannot read Private/ — it is gitignored and invisible to
every workflow, which is exactly what blocked four stage-8 increments. This file holds surface names,
cadences and dates. No credential, no business identifier, no PII. The private CONTENT (the runbooks
themselves) stays in Private/, the owner queue in nikatru/; the STRUCTURAL FACTS a guard reads live here.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-ops-register.mjs (schema, coverage, staleness, revert mitigations,
access-path intersection) and tooling/ci/assert-retention-coverage.mjs (the `retention` rows against
the stores actually enumerated from the tree).
`kind`      one of the eight in `_kinds`. Free text here would let a row opt out of every per-kind
rule below by inventing a ninth kind nothing checks.
`cadence`   a duration (`8h`, `1d`, `7d`, `120d`), OR `on-demand` — WHICH REQUIRES A NON-EMPTY
`why` — OR `trigger`, which requires a named `trigger` event. Three kinds, because the
first draft had only the first two and the parked fresh-host drill fits neither: it is
not on a clock and it is not on-demand, it fires when the next Windows machine is set up.
EVERY duration IS BOUNDED BY `_maxCadenceDays` PER KIND, so a row cannot declare its own
ten-year shelf life and pass. `on-demand` is the escape hatch this stage's audit found in
eighteen criteria; the `why` and the printed count are what stop it being free.
`lastDone`  ⚠️ REQUIRED ONLY FOR THE KINDS A HUMAN PERFORMS — `recovery-path`, `revert`, `review`,
`lastDrill` `failure-mode`. THIS IS A DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the drafted 'absent is a failure for
every kind'. A hand-typed `lastDone` on a nightly cron is a date nobody updates: it would
be written once, go stale in a day, and then either fail CI forever or be bumped by hand
in every unrelated commit — which is the 'record that records success unconditionally'
this stage exists to eliminate, wearing a register's clothes. A MACHINE duty must instead
declare `mechanism.record` + `mechanism.failingValue` — a place a reader can go and a
value that reader can find there and go red on. Duties therefore satisfy an XOR: a human
date, or a machine record whose failing value is reachable. Neither is optional.
`mechanism` `.substrate` names WHAT runs it, `.anchor` a repo-relative path THAT MUST EXIST (a
mechanism naming a file that is gone is a mechanism that is gone), `.record` where its
run history is readable, `.failingValue` the value in that record that means FAILED, and
`.readBy` the thing that actually looks. `grep -rn cron_heartbeat` returning zero readers
while the table carried three consecutive red nights is why `.readBy` is a field.
`accessProviders` resolved from `_providers`, NEVER free text. This is the whole of what makes O-14
computable: a `failure-mode` row names the providers it TAKES DOWN, and the recovery row
it points at names the providers it NEEDS — two independently written lists, and the
guard intersects them. The drafted version compared two sets written by the same hand in
the same row, so a row declaring an empty dependency set could never intersect anything.
`source`    `verified` (measured or read from the thing itself) or `unverified` (corroborated only
by secondary sources — the OCI 30-day abandonment clause, the two statutory breach
clocks). The unverified count PRINTS on every run. Never restate an unverified number as
a fact somewhere else in the repo on the strength of its being written down here.
`ownerGated` the row's missing half can only be supplied from a vendor console, a laptop, or the
proprietor's own knowledge. The guard PRINTS these on every run and does not block —
CLAUDE.md's C-6 rule: a guard that blocks all of CI on work only the owner can do gets
disabled, and a disabled guard checks nothing. It is not a waiver: the gap is counted and
named in every single log line, and rows carrying a DATED tripwire fail after that date.
── THREE THINGS THAT ARE SETTLED AND MUST NOT BE RE-LITIGATED HERE ────────────────────────────────
· [ADR 021] backup destination + the deliberate REMOVAL of encryption.
· [ADR 022] pack-signing key custody — paper + .claude/, Shamir NOT required.
· OWNER_QUEUE S-1 — the GitHub PAT stays broad-scoped and never-expiring, deliberately. It is
referenced by no workflow, so it contributes NO `expiring` row at all: out of the domain by
fact, not by policy. Do not add one, and do not add a rotation reminder.

_why: [14]O-7. A deployable surface must be PROBED after it ships, in the job that shipped it — the domain is
derived from `record-deployment.mjs` calls plus every directory under sites/, so deleting a deploy job
cannot be the way to satisfy the check. These two surfaces have no deploy job to add a step to, and that
is a decision rather than an omission: [F-9] rejected migrating the Cloudflare Git-integration sites into
Actions. Their coverage is O-2's external prober, named here so a NEW site arrives unclassified and red
rather than unwatched and quiet.
📌 APPENDED 2026-08-26 — A THIRD ENTRY ARRIVED AND IT IS NOT THE SAME SHAPE AS THE FIRST TWO. The two
above are exempt because there is NO JOB to probe from. `subly-linux-snap` HAS a job; it is exempt
because the surface carries nothing a probe could JOIN ON. The distinction decides the next entry:
"no job" is a fact about this repository and is retired by a workflow, "nothing joinable" is a fact
about a vendor and is retired by a URL. The Play lane was examined in the same pass and came out the
OTHER WAY — it has a job AND a joinable read, so it got a real smoke and NOT an entry here.
📌 APPENDED 2026-08-26 — A FOURTH ENTRY WAS CONSIDERED FOR `build-platforms.yml:release` AND IS DELIBERATELY
NOT HERE. That job records `$environment` and entered this limb's domain only today, when the shared workflow
reader learned to match a QUOTED SHELL VARIABLE; before that it was dropped in silence and the census printed
"7 deploy job(s)" without it. It got a REAL PROBE rather than an entry, and on the Play test rather than the
Snap one: the GitHub API reports every release asset's `digest` as `sha256:<hex>`, MEASURED 2026-08-26 against
a real release (cli/cli v2.92.0, the API digest re-checked with `sha256sum` over the downloaded asset) to be
exactly the sha256 of the bytes the release serves — and dist/SHA256SUMS already carries that number for every
asset this job staged. So the read joins on what THIS RUN PRODUCED, in both directions, and NOT on "a release
exists at this tag", which a release published last month answers just as well. Snap's three grounds all fail
here: the digest is a machine-readable join key, no reviewer stands between `gh release create` and the read,
and the transport is the same REST API the publish already speaks. The probe is the step named "The release
must carry the assets this job just uploaded" in .github/workflows/build-platforms.yml.
_deploySmokeExemptions.site:nikatru: Deployed by Cloudflare Git integration, not by a workflow — there is no job to probe from. Covered by O-2's external prober (tooling/ops/status.mjs) against the hostname enumerated in tooling/monitor-register.json, which is stage 11's derivation and strictly wider than anything this file would restate. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-11. This line read '⚠️ THREE of that register's monitors are still `Ping` rather than `GET`+expectedStatus — nikatru.com (id 4), rajasekarselvam.com (id 5) and Subly web (id 3) — and a Pages project serving a 500 or a blank shell answers a ping … OWNER_QUEUE S-8.' All three were converted on the live instance with the vault GLITCHTIP_TOKEN and one PUT each; tooling/ops/status.mjs now probes 7 of 7 declared hostnames and prints `0 of 7 … are unprobeable`. 🔴 IT WAS NEVER OWNER WORK — the same wrong filing tooling/monitor-register.json records for the two monitors it CREATED on 2026-08-05, repeated on the conversion. ✅ AND THE RESIDUAL IS CLOSED FOR THE TWO HTML SITES, 2026-08-11: monitors 4 and 5 now assert an `expectedBody` — each site's own canonical link tag, which is host-specific and is absent from the 404 these Pages projects serve, so a blank shell or an edge error page no longer passes. Deleting or retargeting that tag also fails the build, because tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs derives the hostname from it; a mere REFORMAT of it does not, because that guard's regex tolerates whitespace and single quotes while the monitor's match is exact. Monitor 3 (Subly web) asserts the built shell's base-href tag, which proves the served bytes are a real flutter build web output and NOT that the app booted: a monitor runs no JavaScript, so that half stays with the nightly e2e. The count in this file was also wrong twice (`Two` until 2026-08-09 against a register carrying three), which is why the number belongs to the printed count and not to this sentence.
_deploySmokeExemptions.site:rajasekarselvam: Same mechanism and the same caveat as site:nikatru: Cloudflare Git integration, no workflow job, covered by O-2's external prober over the delegated hostname set.
_deploySmokeExemptions.subly-linux-snap: 🔴 NOT "stores are slow" — a SPECIFIC surface carries nothing a probe can join on, for three separate reasons, and closing ANY ONE of them retires this entry. (1) THERE IS NO JOIN KEY. `snapcraft upload` documents no machine-readable output, and the REVISION ID is recorded UNSOURCED in tooling/release/submit-snap.mjs (UNSOURCED[0]): `manageRevisions` says a number "can be obtained with the `snapcraft revisions` command", whose output FORMAT is documented on no page fetched. The only value a probe could compare is the snap VERSION — and a version is NOT unique across revisions, so a channel already carrying an earlier revision of the same version answers such a probe correctly while THIS upload shipped nothing. That is green over precisely the failure it exists to catch: the `Ping` finding tooling/monitor-register.json records, repeated on a store. (2) A NEGATIVE READ IS NOT EVIDENCE EITHER, SO THE PROBE CANNOT EVEN FAIL HONESTLY. `--release` takes effect only "if the store review passes"; that review is AUTOMATIC and happens ON UPLOAD; and `need_manual_review` is an enumerated status. So a channel map that does not yet name this upload is a documented, expected state of a GOOD submission, and failing on it would be a false red on the honest path — the 2026-08-04 lesson tooling/ops/post-deploy-smoke.mjs carries in its own header. (3) THERE IS NO TRANSPORT TO READ FROM. Everything this repo sends to the store goes through `snapcraft`, because UNSOURCED[1] records that the mapping from SNAPCRAFT_STORE_CREDENTIALS onto the store API’s `Authorization: Macaroon root=…, discharge=…` header is not sourced — no request in this tree reaches dashboard.snapcraft.io. And `snapcraft whoami`’s output is ALREADY refused as a parse target in that same file because its format is undocumented; parsing `snapcraft status` would break that rule one command over. 🔴 WHAT COVERS IT INSTEAD: NOTHING DOES, AND THAT IS WRITTEN DOWN AS A GAP RATHER THAN DRESSED AS COVERAGE. The two site: entries above delegate to O-2’s external prober; this one delegates to nobody. The [10]D-9 row this job writes says `in_review` and claims only "we submitted"; the transition to `live` is a separate act nothing in this repository performs. The row is also `served: false` in tooling/channel-register.json and the job has never run, so the gap is real but not yet load-bearing — which is the moment to write it down, not the moment to forget it. WHAT RETIRES THIS ENTRY, and it is one fact either way: a SOURCED machine-readable revision id (UNSOURCED[0]) or the macaroon header mapping (UNSOURCED[1]). Either makes a read-after-upload joinable, and tooling/ops/post-deploy-smoke.mjs then gets a snap limb the way it got a Play one on 2026-08-26. ⚠️ DO NOT COPY THIS ONTO THE PLAY LANE — it was checked on 2026-08-26 and came out the OTHER WAY. .github/workflows/submit-play.yml:submit now runs a real post-deploy smoke, because androidpublisher’s `edits.tracks.list` returns the versionCodes each track carries and the versionCode IS a machine-readable key the upload produces. "The store has a review queue" is true of BOTH channels and settles NEITHER: it is an argument about the LISTING, and the Play probe does not read the listing.

_why: One set, one owner. `hostnames` is [11]E-9's: tooling/monitor-register.json enumerates every host
this factory serves and whether a monitor watches it, derived from the tree by
tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs on every run. This register names the delegate rather than
restating its rows, and its guard fails if the delegate is missing, unparseable, empty, or blind to
a custom domain this repo deploys — so "stage 11 owns it" stays a fact instead of becoming nobody's.
[14]O-4 — WHICH MACHINE IS THIS THING ON. Every `duty` row names the substrate that RUNS it and,
if it is on a clock, an `absenceWatcher` naming the substrate that notices when it STOPS. The
criterion is that the watcher is on DIFFERENT INFRASTRUCTURE, and this map is what makes that a
comparison between two machines instead of between two spellings.
🔴 THE CASE THAT FORCED IT. `oci-cron` and `glitchtip-heartbeat` are different words for THE SAME
ORACLE BOX. The four crontab duties on that host are watched by a GlitchTip instance running on
that host, so the machine failure that silences them silences the watcher AND the mail that would
say so, in the same instant — and the result is indistinguishable from perfect health. A string
comparison would have called that 'different infrastructure' and printed ok. Resolving both sides
to a HOST makes it fail, which is the only reason the limb is worth having.
Every value is a member of `_providers` — the same fixed vocabulary O-14's intersection resolves
against — because free text on the right-hand side is how a comparison stops comparing. A
substrate with no entry here FAILS as 'cannot be checked' rather than passing, and an entry no row
reaches is DELETED rather than kept: a mapping about nothing inflates the domain while resolving
nothing.
⚠️ `renovate-app` resolves to `github` deliberately, and it USED TO BE the one judgement call in
this map. It no longer is: the Mend-hosted App was UNINSTALLED on 2026-09-03 and Renovate now runs
from .github/workflows/renovate.yml, so the duty runs on GitHub Actions and its RECORD (the
Dependency Dashboard issue, the `chore/renovate-*` branches) lives on GitHub too. The mapping is
unchanged and the REASON for it is not: it was a judgement about a third-party host whose record
happened to live here, and it is now simply where the thing runs.
🔴 THE SUBSTRATE NAME IS KEPT ON PURPOSE, not out of inertia. `duty.renovate` is about the BOT
proposing updates; `duty.workflow.renovate.yml` is about the WORKFLOW firing. They fail
independently — the workflow can run green every day while the bot proposes nothing — so renaming
this substrate to `github-actions` would read as one duty where there are two. The map answers
'where would a watcher have to look', which is the question the criterion is about, and both
answers are still `github`.
_portabilityWhy: 🔴 A SUBSTRATE NAMES A ROLE, NEVER A BOX — CHANGED 2026-09-03, AND THE COST OF LEARNING THAT WAS 46
HOURS OF FROZEN DEPLOYMENTS. `oci-cron` and `glitchtip-heartbeat` both resolved to `oci`. GlitchTip
and its whole backup chain moved to the Hostinger box on 2026-09-02, and BOTH mappings silently
became false: measured on 2026-09-03, all four `/opt/glitchtip/*` crons run on Box B (02:00, 02:30,
:41, :17 — matched against the live crontab, not inferred), and GlitchTip itself serves from Box B.
⚠️ THE STALENESS INVERTED A SAFETY CHECK RATHER THAN JUST AGEING. [14]O-4 asks whether a duty's
WATCHER is on different infrastructure from the duty. With both sides pinned to `oci` it kept
reporting the Oracle-box SPOF after the duties had left that box — a true-sounding finding about a
machine that no longer ran them. A map that is wrong in this direction is worse than absent: it
➡️ THE PROPERTY THIS BUYS, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT WITH LIVE USERS: moving a service to another
box is now ONE edit — the host on the right-hand side here. Nothing else in the register, and
nothing in tooling/ops/alarm-chains.json (which keys monitors by `id` since 2026-09-03), needs to
change. Before this, a move required at least four scattered edits and missing any one froze every
merge and both deploys 36 HOURS LATER, with nothing in the failure naming the move.
⛔ NEVER put a box name in a substrate, a monitor name, or a row id. `glitchtip-box-cron` says WHICH
SERVICE'S box; the answer to WHICH MACHINE lives here and only here.

_why: A stage-level ceiling per kind, so a row cannot buy itself an unreachable shelf life. These are
JUDGEMENT CALLS AND ARE RECORDED AS SUCH — none is a vendor SLA and none may be cited as one.
Each is set at the point where 'we last checked' stops being a useful sentence for that kind of
thing, and each is one number, changed deliberately.
[14]O-3's acceptance is 'a query against that mechanism's own record returns a run inside the
last cadence window'. Until 2026-08-06 no query ran: the guard checked that a row NAMED a
`record`, a `readBy` and a `failingValue`, which is a check about prose. Two Windows duties were
returning LastTaskResult = 1 every night while this file exited 0 — the falsifier was true and
the guard was green, because the limb had no domain to range over.
So every duty row on a CLOCK now names a READER, and the reader either queries the record or
prints WHY it cannot. The four honest outcomes are: a successful run inside the window (pass),
a reachable record with no successful run inside the window (FAIL), a reader whose credential or
platform is absent on this runner (print, with the missing thing named), and `unreachable` — the
register's own admission that the record sits on a host nothing in CI or on the laptop can read.
WARNING: `unreachable` IS THE ESCAPE HATCH AND IT IS CAPPED. Declaring every row unreachable would
make this limb green over nothing — the exact defect it replaces — so `_maxUnreachable` is a
CEILING that ratchets DOWN, never a floor on the register's size. Every declared reader must also
own at least one row: a reader nobody uses is code that cannot fail.
`unreadable` IS CAPPED TOO, by `_maxUnreadable`. 8 rows are readable-in-principle here; at 7 the limb
still prints on a laptop holding no tokens, and FAILS the moment the last query goes dark — which is
what a lost GITHUB_TOKEN in ci.yml looks like. `unreadable` routes to `prints`, so until this key existed
that state could not fail no matter how much of the domain it covered.
🔴 BUT A COUNT CANNOT SEE *WHICH* ROW WENT DARK, AND ON THE LINUX RUNNER ONLY 2 OF 13 DO — so the
ceiling above is nowhere near binding while the one genuinely failing duty is one of those 2. A row may
therefore carry `mechanism.recordQuery.lastObserved: { verdict, at, detail }`, its last READABLE verdict.
While that reads `fail`, an unreadable reader on that row is a FAILURE, not a print — and it is cleared
only by editing this file on a host that has just read a success, which the guard then demands.
_maxUnreadableWhy: 🔴 RATCHETED 7 -> 3 ON 2026-09-02, AND THE RATCHET IS THE POINT — this key exists to fall as credentials
and platforms arrive, never to rise when a row goes dark. What changed is that the last reader needing a
PLATFORM (Windows) became a reader needing a CREDENTIAL (GLITCHTIP_TOKEN), and a credential is something
a Linux runner can be given. So every one of the 8 readable rows is now readable in CI, and the measured
count on a good day is 0, not 7.
3 IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN: it is the headroom for ONE network provider going dark, plus one spare. The
8 readable rows sit behind three providers — 6 on the GitHub API, 1 on Cloudflare D1, 1 on GlitchTip —
and a reader that cannot reach its provider returns `unreadable`, which PRINTS. That is the whole reason
ci.yml's standing objection to a CI limb depending on the GlitchTip box is answered rather than ignored:
a Box B outage costs one line of output and never the merge queue. Cloudflare dark costs 1, GlitchTip
dark costs 1, both at once costs 2, and 3 still absorbs it.
⚠️ GITHUB IS THE ONE PROVIDER THIS CEILING DOES NOT ABSORB: its 6 rows would break the ceiling together.
That is deliberate and it is the sentence this key was written for — `FAILS the moment the last query
goes dark, which is what a lost GITHUB_TOKEN in ci.yml looks like`. It is also exactly what happened
before this ratchet: the `The guards must be able to fail` step in ci.yml had NO env block at all, so the
end-to-end test spawned this guard with no credentials of any kind, all 8 readers went dark, and the
ceiling caught it. The remedy was to give that step its tokens, which is what landed with this change —
NOT to raise the number.
⬜ A HOST HOLDING NO CREDENTIALS NOW READS 0 OF 8 AND IS RED, where before it read 1 of 8 (Task Scheduler,
on Windows) and printed. That is a real change and it is stated rather than discovered: run this guard
with `.claude/secrets.env` sourced, or through tooling/scripts/preflight.mjs, which is the same remedy
the repo already applies to every other credentialed guard. `I could not look` must not read as `I looked
and it was fine` on a laptop either.
_recordReaders._windowMultiplierWhy: The same 1.5x the absence watcher uses and for the same reason, written down once in tooling/ops/check-heartbeats.mjs: a window EQUAL to the cadence has zero margin and reports a duty dead on a single late run. One missed run is not an alarm; two are.

glitchtip-heartbeat.queries: GET /api/0/organizations/{org}/monitors/{id}/ then .../checks/ — the newest check with isUp = true, which IS the duty's last successful POST. A monitor that is not a Heartbeat, or a 404 on the declared id, is an ANSWERED query and a hard failure, never a print.
glitchtip-heartbeat.needs: GLITCHTIP_TOKEN in the environment (optionally GLITCHTIP_URL; it defaults to https://glitchtip.nikatru.com)
glitchtip-heartbeat.unreadableOn: any run with no token, and any run where the GlitchTip box cannot be reached — a network failure PRINTS, so a Box B outage costs one line of output and never the merge queue
why: That reader is structurally unreadable on every Linux runner — CI has no Task Scheduler and never will
— and it was tolerable only while the row ALSO held `lastObserved: fail`, because a held failure
classifies as FAILING rather than as a print. Repairing the backup that day correctly cleared the held
failure to `pass`, the row fell through to plain `unreadable`, and the count went to 8 against a ceiling
of 7. BOTH OBVIOUS FIXES ARE WEAKENING: raising the ceiling makes the limb believe itself over a domain
it did not read, and teaching the held-failure branch to accept `PASSING` inverts the evidence — a
self-reported FAILURE is an admission against interest and a self-reported success is not.
The duty already had a record CI can query. It has POSTed to a GlitchTip heartbeat since 2026-07-27 and
this register has named that monitor as its `absenceWatcher` the whole time; nothing new was built on
either box, and no duty changed behaviour. 🔴 IT STILL FAILS WHEN THE HEARTBEAT STOPS, which is the
only property that matters: no POST means no new isUp check, so `lastSuccessMs` ages out of the row's
own cadence window and the verdict is FAIL. That was proven by measurement, not by reading the code —
see `tooling/ci/test/ops-register.test.mjs`, which drives this reader with a stale, a down-only and an
empty check list and asserts RED for each.
KEYED BY `id`, NEVER BY `name`. On the same day, renaming monitor `Oracle box backup chain` to
`GlitchTip backup chain (Box B)` sent `tooling/ops/alarm-chains.json` — which keys by name — COVERAGE
LOST on the next Ops watch run. The id survived that rename untouched. `monitorName` below is carried
for a human reading the row and is deliberately NOT asserted on.

github-run-history.queries: GET /repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow}/runs?event=schedule&status=success&per_page=1 — the newest SUCCESSFUL run for the declared event.
github-run-history.needs: GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN in the environment
github-run-history.unreadableOn: any run with no token — the reason prints and names the missing variable

github-issue-activity.queries: GET /search/issues for the declared title, then its updated_at — the record duty.renovate names.
github-issue-activity.needs: GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN in the environment

cloudflare-d1-heartbeat.queries: POST /accounts/{acct}/d1/database/{db}/query — MAX(created_at) over cron_heartbeat WHERE ok = 1. A row with ok = 0 is NOT a successful run, which is the whole point of reading the table rather than counting rows in it.
cloudflare-d1-heartbeat.needs: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN + CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, and the database_id resolved from the anchored wrangler config

unreachable.queries: nothing, and the row must say why in `mechanism.recordQuery.why`.
unreachable.needs: n/a — this is the register admitting the record is on a host it cannot read
unreachable.unreadableOn: always, by declaration — capped by _maxUnreachable so it cannot become the whole domain

_why: A reader with no member is code that cannot fail, and this file's own error text gives exactly two
remedies: delete it, or point a row at it. This section is the first one, WITH ITS HISTORY, because the
keys here are matched by `readerNames` only when they do NOT start with `_` — so a reader parked in this
object is genuinely undeclared and cannot be used by a row, while the reason it went away survives for
whoever needs it back.
⚠️ THE IMPLEMENTATION IS DELIBERATELY STILL IN `tooling/ci/assert-ops-register.mjs` AND STILL TESTED.
`probeWindowsTasks` / `readScheduledTaskProbe` / `classifyScheduledTaskRow` carry the most expensive
lesson in that file — the `[int]` cast that overflowed on an HRESULT-shaped UInt32 and reported a
RUNNING-AND-FAILING task as one that DID NOT EXIST — and 17 fixture-driven cases still exercise every
branch, so this is dormant code rather than dead code. Re-declaring it is a two-line change on the day a
Windows duty needs reading from the Windows host again.

windows-scheduled-task.needs: the Windows host itself (process.platform === 'win32' and powershell on PATH)

arithmetic (`daysLeft <= leadDays`) has never executed once. A limb whose domain is empty is
green over nothing.
DECISION 2026-08-06 — THE TOLERANCE STAYS, AND STOPS BEING SILENT. Not one of the twelve dates
is knowable in this repository: eight live in a vendor console, one on the Oracle box behind
`openssl x509 -enddate`, one is a non-use clock with no calendar date at all, and two (GST LUT,
Awfis lease) are business values CLAUDE.md forbids mirroring out of the private brain (nikatru/) into this
public file. Requiring a date would therefore either block all of CI on owner-only work
(CLAUDE.md C-6) or invite an invented date — and an invented expiry is worse than a null, because
it reads as coverage and the arithmetic would then pass on a fiction.
What replaces the silence, and both of these CAN fail:
1. `expiryKnownAt` is MANDATORY on every row — the exact place the date is read from. 'Unknown'
becomes 'unread from a named source', which is actionable; deleting the field reddens.
2. `_maxNull` is a CEILING that ratchets DOWN as dates arrive. A thirteenth null expiry fails.
3. The count of rows whose lead-window arithmetic ACTUALLY EXECUTED prints on every run, so
'0 of 12' can never again look like twelve checked expiries.
[14]O-17's acceptance is 'for every store with a retention rule, a query returns zero rows older
than the declared period' — and ZERO rows declare a period, so the deleting-job limb ranges over
the empty set. The same defect as _expiryCoverage above, one requirement over.
DECISION 2026-08-06 — `period-undeclared` STAYS AND IS CAPPED. The period is a policy number:
stage 8 owns WHAT it is, this stage owns the job that makes it true, and an agent inventing one
would be writing policy into a published privacy commitment. But the limb is now ARMED rather
than absent: a row that declares `rule: period` must ALSO name `deletingJob` — the acceptance's
'by a job' half — so the day a period is declared the job requirement lands with it instead of
waiting for somebody to remember to write new code. `_maxUndeclared` is a CEILING that ratchets
down. And the executed-query count prints on every run, so an empty domain announces itself
instead of reading as nineteen checked stores.

the signup KV's period (365 days), retention.kv.nikatru-signups.signup moved to `rule: ttl`, and
the ceiling came down with it. A THIRD undeclared period now fails. Leaving the ceiling at 3
after a gap closes is how a cap silently buys back the room it just gave up — the closed gap
would fund a new one, and the count would still read 'within the ceiling'.

and tooling/monitor-register.json's `closedGap` one level down. A register that erases a row when it
stops being true cannot answer 'how long did this stand, and what made it stop', which is the only
